title: PPO: library vs from-scratch
paper: Schulman et al. 2017, Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
claim: The clipped surrogate objective with GAE gives stable policy-gradient learning, and a faithful from-scratch implementation behaves like the library one.
setup: CartPole-v1, 50000 steps, 5 seeds, identical hyper-parameters for Stable-Baselines3 and our PyTorch PPO (n_steps=256, batch=64, epochs=10, gamma=0.99, lambda=0.95, clip=0.2). Final score = mean return over 20 greedy episodes on held-out env seeds.
result: SB3 PPO final return 500.0 ± 0.0; scratch PPO 495.6 ± 9.8 (max 500). Difference 4.4. Training took 81s vs 74s per run.
verdict_reason: Both means are at least 475 of 500 and differ by 4.4 (0.9% of the maximum return); the rule is: within 5% and both solved.
mismatches: CartPole saturates at 500, so the final score cannot separate two good implementations; the learning curves (below) are the better comparison.
LunarLander is a separate card with a much smaller step budget than it needs; this card is CartPole only.
The paper's experiments are on MuJoCo/Atari; CartPole is a much easier problem.
Greedy evaluation is used for the final score; training curves use stochastic-policy episode returns.
